report:
## Conclusion: No — hydroxychloroquine does **not** reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19

The best available evidence from large randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and meta-analyses of RCTs consistently shows that hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) provides **no mortality benefit** for COVID-19 patients, and may even increase risk.

### Key Evidence

1. **RECOVERY Trial (NEJM, 2020):** The largest RCT on HCQ, with 1,561 patients receiving HCQ and 3,155 receiving usual care, found **no significant difference in 28-day mortality** between the groups. The trial concluded HCQ was not an effective treatment for hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
   — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926

2. **WHO Solidarity Trial:** The WHO confirmed that HCQ "does not result in the reduction of mortality of hospitalised COVID-19 patients, when compared with standard of care," leading to discontinuation of the HCQ arm.
   — https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-hydroxychloroquine

3. **International Collaborative Meta-Analysis (Nature Communications, 2021):** Axfors et al. pooled data from published and unpublished RCTs and found that HCQ was associated with **increased mortality** compared to controls.
   — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22446-z

4. **Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis of RCTs (PMC, 2021):** Kashour et al. analyzed multiple RCTs and found HCQ had **no significant effect on mortality** or viral clearance in COVID-19 patients.
   — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8013604/

### Note on Conflicting Claims
Some websites (e.g., c19early.org) claim HCQ reduces COVID-19 risk, but these analyses heavily rely on observational studies and early-treatment hypotheses rather than rigorous RCT data. The scientific consensus, based on large randomized trials, is clear: HCQ does not reduce COVID-19 mortality.
